publications.title: From Walks to Skeletons: A Reusable Transport Architecture for Interactive Monte Carlo PDE Solvers
publications.summary: Reusable transport structures for efficient PDE queries, changing boundary conditions, and interactive geometry edits.

publications.title: Walk on Multiscale Media: Compiling Editable and Composable Transport Medium Prefabs for Monte Carlo PDE Solvers
publications.summary: Compiling fine-scale heterogeneous transport into editable, composable prefabs for repeated pointwise PDE queries.

publications.title: Walk in Envelopes: Efficient Branching Walk-on-Spheres via Certified Solution Bounds
publications.summary: Certified solution bounds transform branching diffusion to reduce computational cost while preserving unbiasedness.

publications.title: Walk-on-Ambient-Patch: Solver-Adapted Isometric Embeddings for Projected Walk on Spheres
publications.summary: Choosing surface embeddings and projection states jointly to improve stochastic PDE solving on folded geometry.

publications.title: Boundary-Value PDEs Meet Higher-Order Differential Topology-aware GNNs
publications.summary: Higher-order message passing grounded in discrete exterior calculus for boundary-value problems in electromagnetism.

publications.title: Curvature-aware Graph Attention for PDEs on Manifolds
publications.summary: Curvature-aware attention and parallel transport bring intrinsic surface geometry into neural PDE solvers.

news.text: Four new preprints on Monte Carlo PDE solvers: [reusable transport skeletons](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36931), [multiscale media](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35952), [certified solution envelopes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25297), and [solver-adapted embeddings](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15573).
[DEC-HOGNN](https://openreview.net/forum?id=PluDA8DEar) was selected as a **Spotlight** paper at NeurIPS 2025.
[Curvature-aware Graph Attention for PDEs on Manifolds](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/liao25b.html) appeared at ICML 2025.

about.name: Yunfeng Liao
about.description: My research lies at the intersection of **mathematical physics**, **computer graphics**, and **machine learning**. I work on geometry-aware learning and Monte Carlo methods for partial differential equations, advised by [Xiucheng Li](https://xiucheng.org/) at Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen.

research.title: Mathematical Physics
research.body: Exploring the geometry and structure of physical laws, from differential geometry to stochastic representations of PDEs.

research.title: Computer Graphics
research.body: Building geometry-aware, grid-free solvers for physical simulation and creating interactive computational worlds.

research.title: Machine Learning
research.body: Designing neural methods that encode intrinsic geometry, topology, and the structure of physical problems.
